big: Meena, an NRI in Singapore, wants to buy Indian shares, a flat and a pension account. Each has its own door, and some doors are closed to her. The route she picks decides what she can send back.

lines: Can I invest in India the way residents do?
Mostly yes, but through set routes. Shares through a PIS account. Mutual funds through fund houses that accept your country. Residential and commercial property, yes. Farmland, no.

rows: Buy and sell shares through an RBI-approved bank account
Allowed, though some fund houses decline some countries
Residential and commercial yes. Farmland and farmhouses no
An NRI can open a pension account, as per its rules
note: Rules change, so check the current rule with your bank or a qualified adviser.

title: Investing in India
stops: NRIs can buy shares through a PIS account
NRIs may buy agricultural land freely
Some fund houses do not accept some countries
NRIs cannot open an NPS account
caps: A designated bank account approved by the RBI is used.
Farmland, plantations and farmhouses are restricted.
Local rules abroad can limit who a fund house accepts.
NPS is open to NRIs, subject to its rules.

q: Rohan wants to buy Indian shares from Dubai. Which route is used?
opts: A PIS account with an authorised bank
Cash handed to a friend at a broker
Using a resident relative's demat account
A local chit fund run by neighbours
why: The Portfolio Investment Scheme runs via a designated bank.
Cash to a friend skips the rules and leaves no record.
Using a resident's account breaks the rules for NRIs.
A chit fund is not a route to buy listed shares.

q: Meena wants to buy a farmhouse in India. What is the position?
opts: It is allowed freely for every NRI
It is allowed only once in a year
It needs nothing more than a PAN card
why: They are not allowed freely, so this is not the position.
There is no once-a-year rule for such property.
Farmhouses and farmland are restricted for NRIs.
A PAN alone does not open up the restricted category.

q: A fund house declines an application from an NRI in a particular country. What is the likely reason?
opts: The investor's first name or surname
Local rules that bind the fund house
The month of the year of the form
The colour of the paper of the form
why: A name is not the cause of a country-level limit.
Some fund houses avoid some countries due to local laws.
The month of the year has no role in the restriction.
The colour of a form has no link to such a limit.

q: Meena wants a retirement account in India. Which can she consider?
opts: A resident's PPF in her own name
An EPF account with no employer
Nothing at all is open to NRIs
why: PPF has its own rules, and fresh accounts are closed to NRIs.
EPF needs an employer in India, which she may not have.
NPS is open to NRIs, so some options do exist for her.
NRIs can open an NPS account, subject to its rules.

pts: Shares go through a PIS account at an authorised bank.
Farmland, plantations and farmhouses are restricted.
Check if a fund house accepts your country, then invest.
